stakes.purpose: Investment: The Reporting Persons acquired the Series A Preferred Stock for investment purposes. Under the October 22, 2026 Securities Purchase Agreement, Bubble Holdings agreed to invest up to $20 million, purchasing 15,000 preferred shares for $15 million at the initial closing and potentially another 5,000 shares for $5 million at a deferred closing. Deferred investment: The additional $5 million is generally conditioned on the Issuer achieving 2026 net sales of at least $172.5 million and Adjusted EBITDA of at least negative $3 million, together with certain customary closing conditions. Bubble may waive these financial conditions or elect to close early, in which case they are automatically waived. Board representation: While Bubble and its affiliates hold at least 10,000 preferred shares or 8% of the Issuer's common stock on an as-converted basis, Bubble may designate one director to the Board. The Board was increased to eight directors at the initial closing. Voting restrictions: While Bubble owns at least 5%, it generally has discretion over voting or tendering shares representing up to 20% of the Issuer's common stock. Shares above that threshold must generally be voted or tendered proportionately with other shareholders. Additional proportional voting restrictions apply to director elections while Bubble maintains its board designation right. The Swap provides solely for cash settlement and does not give the Reporting Persons the right to acquire, vote or direct the voting of, or dispose of or direct the disposition of, any securities of the Issuer. On October 13, 2026, Czechoslovak Group a.s. issued a press release announcing its investment in the Issuer, in which it stated, among other things, that it intends to be a long-term strategic shareholder of the Issuer and views its investment as an opportunity to explore potential cooperation between Czechoslovak Group a.s. and the Issuer over time. The press release stated that such cooperation could include co-investing in manufacturing or assembly facilities in Europe, partnering on strategic acquisitions, and otherwise seeking to introduce Czechoslovak Group a.s.'s customer relationships to the Issuer to support the Issuer's international growth. stakes.purpose: Item 4 of the Schedule 13D is hereby amended to add the following at the end thereof: On November 13, 2026, the Issuer published a notice convening its annual general meeting of shareholders for December 21, 2026 (the "Annual Meeting"). The notice refers to the pending Petition, but the agenda excludes the matters that are the subject of the Petition. It does include the re-election of Mr. Asaf Shavit, one of the directors whose replacement S.H.N. seeks, as a Class II director. By letter dated November 15, 2026 (the "Agenda Demand"), S.H.N. demanded, pursuant to Section 66(b) of the Israeli Companies Law, 5759-1999 (the "Companies Law") and Article 20(b)(3) of the Issuer's Articles of Association, that the agenda of the Annual Meeting include resolutions (the "Proposed Resolutions"): (i) to remove from office, immediately upon the closing of the Annual Meeting, each of the following currently serving directors: Dr. Ehud Geller, Mr. Efi Cohen-Arazi and Mr. Asaf Shavit; (ii) to elect Ms. Margarita Hirsch Malahovich as a Class I director of the Issuer, for the remainder of the applicable term of such class and until her successor is duly elected and qualified; (iii) to elect Ms. Liat Katzman as a Class II director of the Issuer, as an alternative to the re-election of Mr. Asaf Shavit, for the new term of such class and until her successor is duly elected and qualified; and (iv) to elect Mr. Amos Pickel as a Class III director of the Issuer, for the remainder of the applicable term of such class and until his successor is duly elected and qualified. S.H.N. further demanded that the Issuer publish an amended notice of the Annual Meeting, together with updated proxy materials, that include the Proposed Resolutions, and that it confirm in writing by 9:00 a.m. (Israel time) on November 17, 2026, that it would do so. S.H.N. also stated that, absent such confirmation, it would apply to the Court to amend the Petition. A copy of the Agenda Demand is attached hereto as Exhibit …

Item 4 of the Schedule 13D is hereby amended to add the following at the end thereof: By letters dated October 7, 2026 and October 18, 2026, the Issuer rejected the demand set forth in S.H.N.'s letter to the Issuer dated September 24, 2026 (the "Demand Letter"), asserting, among other things, that under Regulation 7B of the Companies Regulations (Relief for Companies with Securities Listed for Trading on a Stock Exchange Outside of Israel), 5760-2000 (the "Relief Regulations"), such a demand requires a holding of at least 10%. S.H.N. disputes this position because, in its view, the Relief Regulations do not override Article 19(a)(2) of the Issuer's Articles of Association, which entitles holders of at least 5% of the voting rights to demand a special general meeting and has not been amended. Accordingly, on November 2, 2026, S.H.N. filed a petition with the District Court of Tel Aviv (Economic Division) (the "Court") pursuant to Section 65 of the Israeli Companies Law, 5759-1999 (the "Petition"). The Petition seeks an order (i) directing the Issuer to convene a special general meeting to vote on the proposals set forth in the Demand Letter, or, alternatively, at least on the proposed removal of directors, with the Court determining how any resulting vacancies are to be filled; (ii) restricting the Issuer, until such meeting, from taking actions outside the ordinary course of business, including issuing securities (such as under its agreement with YA II PN, Ltd.), and from appointing additional directors; and (iii) requiring the Issuer to pay S.H.N.'s expenses in connection with the Petition, including attorneys' fees.
